profile.namespace: stable tenant-derived user_id; exact match required within each seed/target pair

soft_window_anchor: First immutable database settled_received_at for the successful physical seed. DB clock_timestamp supplies both anchor and admission time. Repeated observation, settlement replay or decision reconstruction cannot renew it.
soft_window_status: application risk assumption to be measured in v2; not an empirically proven TTL or provider lease
estimate: A recently received successful settlement with the same complete native static prefix, parameters and tenant namespace makes cross-branch reuse plausible. The seed itself need not have a positive hit; it may have processed a cold input. Delayed receipt can weaken this estimate and is reported, not recast as provider readiness. Target dispatch never depends on the target's future usage.
integrity: Go reconstructs matching physical calls from the authoritative ledger. Caller-provided verified/availability flags do not authorize dispatch. Simulated and real provider evidence remain isolated.
negative_rule: The latest complete matching extraction with zero aggregate cache hits blocks the prefix for the remainder of that observation's window, including when a newer Answer exists. A subsequent successful matching extraction or aging out of the negative observation can change the estimate; no automatic extra request or renewal of an original window.
observed_scope: 16 protocol requests support limited source text/context bundle attribution. Two production Answer/Extraction pairs shared a 12945-byte native static prefix; extraction followed Answer response by 190.701/173.217ms and each reported 3712 aggregate hit tokens.
limitations: The historical 620-token heuristic removed source text, textual context and some metadata; it is not a pure-document lower bound or exact coverage.
Historical state cannot create a current hot window; every dispatch needs fresh matching observations.
The 5000ms window and increased 2048 output allowance are v2 application choices, not established by the two historic timing samples.
Parameter fingerprints and actual static native prefixes must match within each seed/target pair; calibration methodology does not transfer current cache state across namespaces.
The first implementation supports recent settled seed evidence. Other independently calibrated pre-dispatch bases remain possible; this is not a unique M3 acceptance premise.
Cache estimates can be wrong. All requests reserve cold-price upper cost and settle actual usage; there is no cache-only guarantee or automatic retry.
